# Pandamonium v1.0.60

This train consolidates the first Wave 1 batch under the new release policy: the setup wizard now connects a model without Settings, node agents become first-class registrable endpoints instead of a hardcoded bridge, and the release process itself gains a documented train policy covering cadence, roles, parallel lanes, and emergency hotfixes. The v1.0.59 flush-left sidebar fix is recorded once more only because its release-merge commit falls inside this train's commit range.

## MAD-862 — Release: batch Pandamonium patches and deduplicate identical-SHA publication

### Problem

Stable releases were cut one fix at a time: six releases in roughly 21 hours, each repeating the same PR checks, main checks, tag workflows, signed assets, image builds, installed acceptance, and notes ceremony. Release notes summarized by PR, so a consolidated pull request could visually collapse many Linear issues into one item, and parallel agent lanes competed for tags and version files.

### Implementation

Adds `docs/release-train.md` and links it from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: at most one planned train per day (or one operator-requested train), emergency hotfixes reserved for data loss, updater failure, security exposure, or production-stopping regressions, exactly one release manager per train as the sole writer of merges, version bumps, tags, and notes, and explicit parallel-lane rules (one issue per branch and PR, isolated worktrees, serialized hot files, rebase before review, no tagging or publishing from implementation lanes). Commit `97034231`; PR #180.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. Operator-visible process change: a finished batch now ships as one signed, documented train instead of one release per fix, and concurrent agent lanes have a written conflict protocol.

### Verification

PR #180 passed the required PR check set (PR description and title gates, gitleaks, Python syntax and tests, JS syntax, hadolint, actionlint, zizmor, pip-audit, Docker Compose config, Voice Orb focused and browser suites) with a docs-only diff. Remaining MAD-862 criteria — diff-aware per-PR checks, the complete suite on the release candidate plus nightly drift, and single multi-arch digest promotion — stay tracked in Linear under this issue and are not claimed as complete here.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Documentation only: no dependency, runtime, API, database, or data change. The policy binds immediately through the release manager role; the CI automation for per-PR check selection and image digest promotion remains the tracked work in MAD-862.

## MAD-923 — Onboarding 2/3: wizard model step — connect a model without Settings

### Problem

The guided setup wizard from MAD-922 had a required "Give it a brain" step but no way to complete it: a non-technical admin still had to leave onboarding and open Settings to connect a model. The only working connect logic lived inside the `/setup` chat slash command.

### Implementation

Extracts the `/setup` connect logic into a DOM-free shared helper, `static/js/modelConnect.js` (provider detection, credential extraction, chat URL normalization, local-probe flags, `connectDetectedEndpoint`, honest result messages), and rewires the existing chat flow to consume it without behavior change. Fills the wizard model step with three inline paths: paste an API key or provider URL (detect provider, validate, test live), scan this machine for a local model server through `GET /api/discover` with per-row Add using the settings scan pattern, or skip for now. Successful connects show a live model-count confirmation, refresh the model list, mark the default chat model through the existing endpoint-create behavior, and auto-continue; failures render human next-steps copy and never expose raw backend codes. Commits `56bfb8b0`, `dff703ac`, `39fea896`; PR #182.

### Product value and UI visibility

The wizard now completes the model step end to end: the API-key/provider-URL form, the machine scan with per-row Add, the skip path, the model-count confirmation, and the error copy all reuse Pandamonium's existing settings/composer visual language, CSS variables, and button classes. A screenshot was recorded for release review and is attached to the Linear issue.

### Verification

Red-first and focused coverage: 26 Python checks passed (`test_setup_wizard_ui.py`, `test_slash_setup_provider_aliases.py`, `test_setup_llamacpp_hint_js.py`, `test_local_endpoint_api_key_js.py`, `test_identity_first_run.py`, `test_brand_frontend.py`), the shared helper's Node test passed (detection, URL normalization, probe flags, success, sanitized HTTP 400 detail, timeout, saved-but-empty), and the setup-wizard browser spec passed 9 tests plus 3 `ui-polish` tests. `node --check` and `py_compile` clean; PR #182 CI green including the PR description and title gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only change: no dependency addition, no endpoint API contract change, and the `/setup` chat flow keeps its existing behavior and tests. Generic `sk-` keys still require naming the provider, matching the chat flow's no-guess policy. No live third-party provider was reachable during verification; acceptance is proven against stubbed endpoint and discovery APIs plus the unchanged server-side default-assignment path.

## MAD-934 — Agents: register node agents as endpoints and remove the hardcoded PC Codex bridge requirement

### Problem

The PC Codex bridge was a hardcoded worker: a user could not directly register another node agent without an agent's help, and the Friday/pc-codex binding lived in code and environment flags rather than data.

### Implementation

Adds a first-class `agent` endpoint kind alongside model endpoints in `routes/model_routes.py`, persisted through an additive `agent_meta` JSON column on `model_endpoints` with an idempotent `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` migration in `core/database.py` (model endpoints leave it NULL). Adds a one-time pairing flow (the bridge displays a code or token; the user pastes it into Pandamonium and the connection is tested live) with fail-closed handling for invalid, unauthorized, unreachable, and incompatible pairings, and no secret leakage in status payloads. Migrates the existing Friday/pc-codex binding into a registered agent endpoint row so the binding is data, not code, while keeping the existing worker behavior, task APIs, and voice routing intact. Agent endpoints appear in Added Models with node grouping and in the composer/model picker as agent targets with honest availability. Commits `3e247808`, `6db0e62d`, `ed0bc72d`, `3dca587d`, `b8dc637e`, `d2cabb42`, `93c72279`; PR #184.

### Product value and UI visibility

A node agent can now be registered from the existing Add Models flow with label, node URL, bridge protocol, pairing token, status, and enablement, and the registered agent is visible in Added Models and selectable in the composer/model picker. The UI reuses existing settings cards, inputs, badges, and CSS variables; no parallel component patterns were introduced. A screenshot was recorded for release review and is attached to the Linear issue.

### Verification

Focused suites: registration, pairing, migration, availability, and redaction 19 passed; routing and picker availability 8 passed; node UI 2 passed; browser spec 2 passed; a 52-file related regression set 988 passed; full local suite 5849 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed. `py_compile` and `node --check` clean; PR #184 CI green, including Python tests, Voice Orb focused and browser jobs, gitleaks, JS syntax, and the PR description and title gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

The `agent_meta` column is additive and nullable; reverting the code leaves it harmlessly unused, and orphaned agent rows can be deleted from Added Models. No new dependency. Only the `codex-bridge` protocol is accepted in this pass, and legacy migration fires when the existing PC Codex environment flag is set; once migrated, the database row (including node workspaces) is the source of truth. A live bridge was not reachable during verification: pairing and the browser flow were proven with stubbed HTTP transports, and registered-agent voice replies currently arrive via task events rather than the pc-codex-only foreground wait.

## MAD-944 — Projects: keep chat and project rows flush left in the Chats sidebar

### Problem

Live acceptance of MAD-920 on v1.0.56 found the hidden move handle still occupying layout space in every chat and project row, indenting folder icons and chat labels by about 18px relative to the Projects label and the other sidebar rows.

### Implementation

Shipped in v1.0.59 as commit `740a1ab4` (PR #175): the chat and project drag handles are absolutely positioned over the row's left edge with zero layout width and `pointer-events: none` at rest, revealing on hover, `:focus-visible`, drag, or `body.rearrange-mode`. This train's commit range includes the v1.0.59 release-merge commit (`945468fa`) whose message names MAD-944, so the outcome is recorded here once for provenance only.

### Product value and UI visibility

The Chats section reads like the rest of the sidebar: project folder icons line up with the Projects label and chat rows keep only their folder indent, while the move handle appears exactly when the row is hovered, focused for keyboard reordering, dragged, or rearrange mode is on.

### Verification

As verified for v1.0.59: the hidden-handle source guard in `tests/test_projects_in_chats.py` asserts the absolute, zero-layout handle with no flex-shrink gutter; `tests/browser/mad-820-sidebar-organization.spec.js` asserts the geometry; live CT103 v1.0.59 acceptance confirmed the installed stylesheet carries the zero-layout rule and the Linear issue is closed with that evidence.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only change: no dependency, API, database, or data migration. Session and project ordering, bindings, and drag/keyboard reorder behavior are unchanged.
